paragraphs.text: # dsh-rea-toolkit
**One-line value:** after installing, your DeepSeek Harness agent gains the full REA (Reverse Engine
er Anything) toolset — evidence-backed static analysis of JavaScript/Electron applications, browser
extensions, ASAR archives, .NET assemblies, native binaries, SQLite databases, WASM, EVM bytecode, a
nd more — as native `mcp__rea__*` tools.
## What it does
This bundle packages the **REA v6.7.0 runtime** (`dist/`, verified Windows native artifact, skills,
and the exact dependency lockfile) together with a DeepSeek Harness **configuration-only MCP bundle*
* that registers REA's stdio MCP server through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`. REA analyzes targets
**locally**; results include per-conclusion evidence and limitations.
Typical agent prompts after install:
- *"Analyze the extracted extension at `D:/apps/legacy-ext` and list its modules, IPC channels and g

ateway endpoints with evidence."*
- *"Inspect this Electron app's ASAR and explain how the renderer
talks to the main process."*
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then, inside the installed bundle directory, run the bootstrap **once** and restart DeepSeek Harness
hen, inside the installed bundle directory, run the bootstrap **once** and restart DeepSeek Harness:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The bootstrap: discovers a suitable Node.js (22.19+/24.11+/26+), verifies the bundled REA runtime, i
nstalls REA's exact production dependencies from the shipped lockfile, persists `DSH_REA_HOME` / `DS
H_REA_NODE` at user scope, and runs REA's own `mcp doctor`.
**Resolution contract** (see `cordis.patch.yml`):
| Environment | Behavior |
| `DSH_REA_NODE` + `DSH_REA_HOME` set | Absolute node + bundled, validated REA runtime (works with n

o system Node on PATH) |
| `DSH_REA_HOME` only | `node` from PATH + bundled runtime |
| Neither set
| `npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 mcp` fetches the official runtime from npm |
Without any setup the bundle still installs safely — you simply get no REA tools until the bootstrap
runs (or npm/npx is available).
## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness (DSH) with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` (shipped profile package).
- Windows 10+
x64 (uses the bundled verified `rea-windows-x64.node` Node-API addon; loader checks version/ABI/arc
hitecture/SHA-256 at load), Linux x64, macOS (Apple silicon: JS analysis lanes; native binary lanes

per REA docs).
- Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ (auto-discovered by the bootstrap; the bundled DeepSeek H
arness runtime qualifies).
## Permissions & external services
- **Local-only analysis:** REA reads the target files/directories you point it at and writes nothing

outside its own analysis sessions. It does not upload targets anywhere.
- **Network:** only optiona
l — npm registry (first bootstrap / npx fallback) and analysis targets that the agent explicitly ask

s to inspect over the network (e.g., a website URL via the browser lane).
- **Execution scope:** sta
tic analysis lanes do not run the analyzed application. Runtime capture lanes (browser observation,
process capture, frida) run only when an agent workflow explicitly invokes them, with the harness us

er's permissions.
- **Ambient secrets** (`*TOKEN*`, `*KEY*`, …) are scrubbed from the MCP child envi
ronment by the Harness MCP client.
## License

- Wrapper (bundle, scripts, manifest): **MIT** — see LICENSE.
- Bundled REA runtime: **MIT** — see r
untime/rea/LICENSE, runtime/rea/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and runtime/rea/DISCLAIMER.md. REA is for law
ful analysis of software you own or are authorized to examine.
## Category
Development & Operations (secondary: Tools & Capabilities).
## Notes

- REA upstream: <https://github.com/morluto/rea> (not affiliated with this bundle).
- Native deep-an
alysis engines (Hopper / Ghidra / IDA) are bring-your-own and optional; JavaScript/extension analysi

s needs none of them.
- The `index.js` `apply(ctx)` export is an inert plugin-spec compliance shim;
the bundle is configuration-only.
